kernels.definition: Market equilibrium occurs at the price where the quantity demanded by buyers equals the quantity supplied by sellers.

definitionAnchor.quote: the price where the quantity demanded by buyers equals the quantity supplied by sellers

facts.text: At the equilibrium price the opposing pressures of demand and supply are balanced and the price has no tendency to change.

To minimize the cost of goods purchased
To select the most expensive bundle available
To ensure all goods are equally valued
mcItems.ex: To maximize utility subject to a budget constraint

mcItems.q: At the optimal choice, what condition must be met regarding utility?
op: Utility can be increased without exceeding the budget
Utility cannot be increased without exceeding the budget
Utility is maximized when the budget is fully exhausted
Utility is independent of the budget constraint
mcItems.ex: Utility cannot be increased without exceeding the budget

mcItems.q: Which condition describes demand that is elastic?
op: The absolute value of the elasticity is less than one
The absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one
The absolute value of the elasticity is equal to one
The absolute value of the elasticity is zero
mcItems.ex: Demand is elastic when the absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one.

mcItems.q: Which factor primarily determines the elasticity of demand?
op: The absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one
The percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price
The availability of close substitutes
Necessities tend to have inelastic demand
mcItems.ex: The availability of close substitutes is a primary determinant of elasticity. Demand is elastic when the absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one. This is because consumers have few substitutes for necessities.

mcItems.q: When the price of a good increases, what happens to the quantity consumers are willing and able to purchase, assuming all other factors remain unchanged?
op: The quantity demanded increases
The quantity demanded decreases
The demand curve shifts to the right
The demand curve shifts to the left
mcItems.ex: The quantity demanded decreases because a change in price causes a movement along the demand curve.

mcItems.q: If consumer tastes change, how is the demand curve affected?
op: The quantity demanded moves along the curve
The demand curve shifts to the right
The demand curve shifts to the left
The demand curve remains stationary
mcItems.ex: The demand curve shifts to the left because a change in tastes causes the curve to shift.

mcItems.q: How does the wage-price spiral function in terms of feedback?
op: A it operates as negative feedback, dampening the initial price changes
B it functions as positive feedback, amplifying the initial change
C it represents a stable equilibrium where price and wage levels remain constant
D it is a system where initial shifts are immediately reversed by consumer behavior
mcItems.ex: The wage-price spiral is positive feedback: an initial change is amplified rather than damped. This is correct because the claims state that the wage-price spiral is positive feedback: an initial change is amplified rather than damped.

mcItems.q: What describes the mechanism of a wage-price spiral?
op: A self-reinforcing cycle where rising prices cause workers to demand higher wages, and higher工资
A process where initial changes are dampened over time
A situation where equilibrium is reached quickly
A scenario where positive feedback drives the system toward stability
mcItems.ex: A self-reinforcing cycle where rising prices cause workers to demand higher wages, and higher wage costs lead firms to raise prices further.

keyTerms.df: The study of how individuals select goods to maximize their satisfaction within financial limits.
keyTerms.eg: A student chooses to buy a textbook or a movie ticket based on their available money.
keyTerms.mi: This theory suggests that a consumer's satisfaction is determined solely by the absolute quantity of goods they possess.
keyTerms.cx: The systematic process by which a person decides which combination of items to purchase given their spending capacity.

keyTerms.df: The limitation on the total expenditure a consumer can make on various goods.
keyTerms.eg: If a person has $100, the budget constraint limits them to spending no more than $100.
keyTerms.mi: The budget constraint dictates that a consumer must spend every dollar they have, regardless of the value of the goods.
keyTerms.cx: The boundary defining the set of all possible combinations of goods a consumer can afford.

It perfectly mirrors the complexity of the real-world situation.
It includes all possible variables for complete accuracy.
It is a complete and exact depiction of reality.
